review: 702.107a-2 stack-not-empty: delta left Shock in B's hand and Mountain untapped while saying Shock was on the stack; restated it as B having cast Shock by tapping Mountain.

scenarios.title: Outlast taps the creature and puts a +1/+1 counter on it when it resolves

setup.notes: Salt Road Patrol is a 2/5 with outlast {1}{W}.

decisions: A activates Salt Road Patrol's outlast ability, paying {1}{W} with both Plains and tapping Salt Road Patrol.
Both players pass; the ability resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Salt Road Patrol is tapped and has one +1/+1 counter after the ability resolves; it is 3/6.

variants.label: creature-gone
variants.delta: In response, B casts Doom Blade targeting Salt Road Patrol, tapping both Swamps.
variants.expected: Doom Blade destroys Salt Road Patrol, which goes to A's graveyard. The outlast ability resolves and puts no counter anywhere.

scenarios.title: Outlast can be activated only as a sorcery and only while the creature can tap
decisions: A considers activating Salt Road Patrol's outlast ability ({1}{W}, {T}) with an empty stack.

variants.label: combat
variants.delta: The step is beginning_of_combat instead of main1.
variants.expected: Activating outlast is not legal because it is not a main phase.

variants.label: stack-not-empty
variants.delta: B has cast Shock targeting A (tapping Mountain) and it is on the stack, with A holding priority.
variants.expected: Activating outlast is not legal because the stack is not empty.

variants.label: summoning-sick
variants.delta: Salt Road Patrol came under A's control this turn (summoning_sick true).
variants.expected: Activating outlast is not legal because the {T} cost cannot be paid.

variants.label: already-tapped
variants.expected: Activating outlast is not legal because the {T} cost cannot be paid.

variants.label: one-land
variants.expected: Activating outlast is not legal because {1}{W} cannot be paid.
